description: Single Minecraft world integrating Cheyenne Mountain Complex (NORAD), SubTropolis (underground business park), and Houston Tunnel System (underground pedestrian network). One descent, three worlds, 800 million years of geology. NO-RAVINE REWORK: the V-shaped ravine has been dropped. The mountain is now one continuous range with a horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200.
rework_note: 2026 rework: V-shaped ravine dropped, replaced with one continuous mountain range. The horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200 separates upper granite (Y=200 to Y=800) from lower limestone (Y=0 to Y=200, with limestone continuing below the city to Y=-100 to host SubTropolis). The composite terrane plaque has moved from the (deleted) ravine bottom to the service tunnel contact crossing, where it is geologically honest rather than narrative fiction. The Grand Avenue is a straight line in the coastal plain. The return route is funicular + road (no skybridge, no ravine to cross). The 25-ton blast door and the Cheyenne outer portal are at the contact elevation Y=200 on the south face of the mountain (not at a ravine wall). The service tunnel is an ascending inclined minecart bore, climbing from Y=0 at the SubTropolis end to Y=200 at the Cheyenne end on a 3.33:1 grade.

scale.notes: 1:1 globally per discussion-notes Decision 1. Mountain peak at Y=800 represents a 2:1 vertical compression of the real 2,915m Pikes Peak, consistent with the 01-masterplan's 1,450-block mountain. All other dimensions (SubTropolis chamber, public shaft length, service tunnel length, city footprint) are 1:1 against real-world references. The horizontal contact at Y=200 is real geology (granite plutons push up through limestone in mountain ranges worldwide).

recommended_mod: CubicWorld or similar with at least 2,048 block build height (vanilla 384 is insufficient)

world_origin.description: Center of the city, at ground level. Y=0 is the city surface and the mountain base. Vanilla sea level convention is not used.

footprint.description: 800 x 600 horizontal x 800 vertical (X x Z x Y)

granite_intrusion.description: Upper portion of the mountain. Pink-grey Pikes Peak syenogranite (1.08 Ga). Hosts the Cheyenne chamber at Y=250-400. Spruce/dark-oak forest on lower slopes, snow line Y=700-800, antenna arrays on ridgeline.

limestone_body.description: Lower portion of the mountain. Cream-grey Bethany Falls limestone (270 Ma). The limestone continues below the city to Y=-100 to host the SubTropolis chamber. Oak/birch forest on lower slopes.

horizontal_contact.description: Horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200. Visible as a 1-2 block color-change ring on the mountain's south face (800 blocks E-W). Exposed in the service tunnel walls at the contact crossing at (-40, 200, -360). Real geology: granite plutons push up through limestone in mountain ranges worldwide.

mountain_layout.ravine_dropped: The V-shaped ravine from the previous design has been dropped. The mountain is a single continuous mass. Drainage from the mountain is via small seasonal streams on the south face that flow into the coastal plain.

public_shaft.cross_section_components: 5x5 inner lift core + 1-block emergency stair (west) + 1-block service chase (east)

service_tunnel.cross_section_components: 4x4 inner minecart rail corridor + 1-block utility strip (north) + 1-block emergency-escape corridor (south, yellow stripe)
service_tunnel.alignment: straight, no curves, climbing 3.33:1 from Y=0 to Y=200
service_tunnel.mode: minecart rail (1-block gauge, single track, powered rail every 4 blocks in climbing section)

granite_peak_summit.description: Single peak, apex of the granite intrusion. Pikes Peak-style triangle. 1,800+ ft (549+ blocks) of solid granite above the chamber at Y=250.

horizontal_contact_line.description: The horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200, visible as a clear color line on the mountain's south face for the full 800-block E-W extent.

mountain_south_face.description: The dramatic south face of the mountain, visible from the city. The contact at Y=200 is the visual signature of the face.

city_center.description: Center of the 138m x 138m downtown in the wide flat valley at the mountain base. World origin.

city_footprint.description: 138m x 138m, with 80m-tall towers. In the wide flat valley between the mountain (north) and the coastal plain (south).

combined_complex_transit_hub_plaza.description: 20x20 block plaza at the NE corner of the city, where the public shaft entrance is located. Stone brick and quartz accents, fountain, benches. The 7x7 glass-and-steel pavilion is at the center.

public_shaft_top_pavilion.description: NE corner of the city, 7x7 glass-and-steel pavilion. Guard booth, turnstile, T-marker, 'SubTropolis - Public Access' sign, dual-use 'EMPLOYEE ENTRANCE / EMERGENCY EGRESS' sign. Centerpiece #4.

public_shaft_mid_landing.description: At Y=-50, the G-Cans observation room. 7x7 with a single 3x3 glass window on south face looking out at the city's underground utility corridor (parallel 7x7 shaft 5 blocks east at x=65). Contains one labelled block of exposed limestone (Bethany Falls Limestone, 270 Ma, Pennsylvanian). Centerpiece #2.

public_shaft_bottom_lobby.description: SE corner of SubTropolis chamber, where the mechanical lift lands. Security gate, turnstile, 'Welcome to SubTropolis' channel-letter sign, 'Hunt Midwest SubTropolis - Industrial Complex, Est. 1964' sign, 'HELSINKI 5,500' carved block (Easter egg #4), iron door opening onto Hushpuckney Avenue.

service_tunnel_start_subtropolis_end.description: NW corner of SubTropolis chamber, on the south face of the mountain, in the limestone at city level. Open entrance with 'U.S. Space Force - Authorized Personnel Only' sign, 1-block security gate, turnstile. 'Service Tunnel - Inspired by the Gotthard Base Tunnel' sign with SBB CFF FFS logo (Easter Egg #3). The minecart rail starts here and climbs 200 blocks of elevation to the contact at Y=200 over the first 60 blocks of the tunnel.

service_tunnel_contact_crossing.description: INSIDE THE SERVICE TUNNEL at the horizontal contact elevation Y=200, where the tunnel walls transition from cream limestone to pink granite. The COMPOSITE TERRANE PLAQUE is here (centerpiece #3, Easter Egg #1) in a 3x5 alcove carved into the upper (granite) wall. 1x2 carved-stone plaque (chiseled calcite + chiseled stone brick) lit by 1 redstone lamp, with 6-7 oak signs of geological text. 1-block-wide cobblestone + calcite breccia strip on the floor (Easter Egg #8). Geologically honest at a real geological boundary.

service_tunnel_end_cheyenne_outer_portal.description: On the south face of the mountain, in the granite, at the contact elevation Y=200. Concrete-and-granite frame, 25-ton blast door recessed in a 4-block side branch, 4-block concrete-and-granite checkpoint corridor, guard booth, 'U.S. Space Force - Authorized Personnel Only' sign (Easter Egg #6). Centerpiece #6.

blast_door_25_ton.description: At the Cheyenne outer portal, service tunnel terminus. 3-block-thick iron door, 6-block-wide x 12-block-tall (scaled 2x per Cheyenne masterplan) in a quartz-stair frame. Visible from the approaching minecart. Centerpiece #1.

composite_terrane_plaque.description: Inside the service tunnel at the contact crossing. 1x2 carved-stone plaque in a 3x5 alcove carved into the upper (granite) wall. Plaque: chiseled calcite (limestone half) + chiseled stone brick (granite half). Lit by 1 redstone lamp. 6-7 oak signs of geological text. Centerpiece #3 and Easter Egg #1. The build's Telling Detail - geologically honest (at a real geological boundary, not narrative fiction).

subtropolis_horizontal_portal.description: 4x5 block opening in the limestone hillside at the south face of the mountain, at city level (Y=0). 'Hunt Midwest SubTropolis - Authorized Vehicles' sign, 'World's Largest Underground Business Complex' sign (Easter Egg #5), vehicle gate, 6-block-wide asphalt switchback road to the city. A 1-block-wide polished diorite band directly above the frame (the contact plane, visible as a pink stripe over the cream portal at Y=200). Centerpiece #5.

cheyenne_chamber_center.description: Vertical center of the Cheyenne chamber (4.5 acres, 1,319 springs, 15 buildings).

funicular_start.description: At the Cheyenne outer portal, where the funicular rail begins. Part of the 2-mode surface return route (funicular + road, no skybridge).

funicular_end_granite_summit.description: At the granite summit. The 'Three Sites, One Mountain' sign (Easter Egg #2) and the rock identification chart (Easter Egg #9) and the summit observation platform (7th centerpiece) are placed at the funicular station.

paved_road_start_granite_summit.description: At the granite summit, where the funicular arrives and the paved switchback down the south face begins.

paved_road_end_city_center.description: At the Combined Complex Transit Hub plaza, where the road arrives at street level.

coastal_plain_south_edge.description: Far south edge of the world, where the Grand Avenue terminates and the world-edge pier is located.

grand_avenue_start.description: South end of the Grand Avenue, at the world edge. The 'old town' section (stone brick, first 350 blocks).

grand_avenue_end.description: North end of the Grand Avenue, at the city NE corner. The 'new city' section (granite-and-glass, final 75 blocks).

public_shaft.cross_section_components: 5x5 inner lift core + 1-block emergency stair (west) + 1-block service chase (east)
public_shaft.mode: mechanical lift with visible emergency stair through glass wall

mid_landing.description: 7x7 G-Cans-style observation room with single 3x3 glass window on south face looking out at city's underground utility corridor. One labelled block of exposed limestone (Bethany Falls Limestone, 270 Ma, Pennsylvanian). 4-line info sign. Oak stairs bench. Iron door 2nd exit to emergency stair.

public_shaft.binding_decision: Discussion Topic 3, Decision 3. Cross-section 7x7 (5x5 lift + 2-block outer ring), mechanical lift primary, 100-block descent Y=0 to Y=-100, mid-level observation landing at Y=-50.

service_tunnel.cross_section_components: 4x4 inner minecart rail corridor + 1-block utility strip (north) + 1-block emergency-escape corridor (south, yellow stripe)
service_tunnel.alignment: straight, no curves, climbing 3.33:1 from Y=0 to Y=200
service_tunnel.mode: minecart rail (1-block gauge, single track, powered rail every 4 blocks in climbing section)

climb_profile.first_60_blocks: Climbing from Y=0 to Y=200 at 3.33:1 grade. Walls are cream limestone (smooth stone). Powered rails every 4 blocks.
climb_profile.last_60_blocks: Lateral at Y=200. Walls transition from cream limestone to pink granite at the contact crossing (~60-65 blocks in at -40, 200, -360). The remaining 55-60 blocks are in the granite.

contact_crossing.description: At the contact elevation Y=200, where the tunnel walls transition from cream limestone to pink granite. The composite terrane plaque is here. Thrust-fault breccia visible in the walls. The geological moment of the build, geologically honest (not narrative fiction).
contact_crossing.plaque_text: Thrust Fault Contact - Pikes Peak Granite (1.08 Ga) overthrust on Bethany Falls Limestone (270 Ma). The contact is exposed at the surface on the south face of the mountain at Y=200, and crossed by this tunnel.

blast_door_position.description: 25-ton blast door at the Cheyenne outer portal, recessed in a 4-block side branch. 3-block-thick iron door in a 6-block-tall x 6-block-wide quartz stair frame. SCALED 2X per the Cheyenne masterplan: actual size 3 thick x 6 wide x 12 tall.

service_tunnel.binding_decision: Discussion Topic 4, Decision 4 (REWORKED for no-ravine). Cross-section 6x6 (4-block minecart rail + 2-block utility strip), minecart rail mode, 120 blocks, climbing 3.33:1 from Y=0 to Y=200. 25-ton blast door at Cheyenne end at (0, 200, -420). Geological moment at the contact crossing at (-40, 200, -360). REWORKED: tunnel is now an ascending inclined minecart bore in the mountain, climbing through the contact at Y=200, NOT a flat tunnel under a ravine.

funicular.mode: funicular rail on the east or west face of the granite intrusion (steep climb)
funicular.description: REPLACES the previous 'funicular + skybridge' 2-stage return. The funicular now goes directly from the outer portal to the granite summit; no skybridge crossing is needed because there is no ravine to span.

summit_road.mode: paved stone-brick road switchback down the south face of the mountain
summit_road.description: Switchback down the south face of the mountain, through the limestone base, to the city. ~6 switchbacks, ~800 blocks of lateral distance, 800 blocks of elevation loss. Arrives at the Combined Complex Transit Hub plaza.

inter_site_connections.skybridge_dropped: The skybridge from the previous design has been dropped. There is no ravine to span, and the mountain is a single mass. The funicular + road return is the cleaner 2-mode resolution.

outer_portal_position.description: On the south face of the mountain, in the granite, at the contact elevation Y=200. NEW: outer portal placement updated for the no-ravine rework (was at Y=0 in the ravine wall in the previous design).

cheyenne_mountain.binding_notes: Chamber geometry, spring layout, and J-curve internal detail are owned by 01-masterplan. Combined complex adds the outer portal placement at (0, 200, -420) on the south face of the mountain, the second 25-ton blast door (scaled 2x) at the service tunnel terminus, the funicular from outer portal to granite summit, and the 'U.S. Space Force' sign. The outer portal is at the contact elevation Y=200 (not at a ravine wall as in the previous design). No amendment to 01-masterplan required.

horizontal_portal_position.description: On the south face of the mountain, at city level. NEW: position unchanged from previous design at Y=0, but the surrounding context is now the south face of the continuous mountain (not a ravine wall). A 1-block-wide polished diorite band directly above the frame at Y=200 is the visible surface expression of the contact.

service_tunnel_entrance_position.description: NW corner of the chamber, where the minecart rail exits to the service tunnel. The rail climbs from Y=0 to the contact elevation Y=200 over the first 60 blocks of the service tunnel at 3.33:1 grade.

subtropolis.binding_notes: Chamber geometry and pillar grid are owned by 02-masterplan. The 5x5 spec is preserved as the public shaft lift core (the 7x7 is the architectural envelope). Combined complex adds the public shaft landing, the horizontal portal at (0, 0, -300) at city level, and the service tunnel entrance at (-100, 0, -300). No amendment to 02-masterplan required.

houston_tunnel.binding_notes: 24-block sample owned by 03-masterplan. Combined complex adds the public shaft buffer block in the SE corner (already flagged in 03-masterplan) and the T-marker at the public shaft entrance. No amendment to 03-masterplan required.

granite_peak.notes: Pikes Peak syenogranite analogue. Pink-grey. The primary palette for the granite intrusion (above Y=200).

limestone_body.notes: Bethany Falls limestone analogue. Cream-grey. The primary palette for the limestone body (Y=0 to Y=200, extending below to Y=-100).

city_above_ground.notes: Houston-style above-ground palette. Sun-bleached, glass-and-quartz, skybridges.

houston_tunnel.notes: Beige VCT tile (white wool), fluorescent 4000K (sea lantern), T-marker red the only consistent color across the civilian layer.

public_shaft_top_pavilion.notes: Y=0. Glass-and-steel pavilion. Light level 15 (daylight). Centerpiece #4.

public_shaft_upper.notes: Y=-3 to Y=-50. Cool blue/gray. Houston above-ground construction. Light level 12.

public_shaft_mid_landing.notes: G-Cans observation room. Single 3x3 glass window on south face looking out at utility corridor 5 blocks east. One labelled limestone block (Bethany Falls Limestone, 270 Ma). Light level 12. Centerpiece #2.

public_shaft_lower.notes: Y=-50 to Y=-100. Walls transition gray concrete -> smooth stone -> calcite. Warm cream. SubTropolis palette begins to dominate. Light level 12.

public_shaft_bottom_lobby.notes: Y=-100. SE corner of SubTropolis chamber. Welcome to SubTropolis sign, Hunt Midwest - Est. 1964 sign, dual-use info sign. Easter egg #4 lives here.

service_tunnel_subtropolis_end.notes: SubTropolis end of service tunnel at (-100, 0, -300). Open entrance. 'SERVICE TUNNEL -> CHEYENNE / U.S. Space Force' sign. Easter egg #3 lives here.

service_tunnel_limestone_section.notes: First 60 blocks of the service tunnel from SubTropolis end, climbing 3.33:1 from Y=0 to Y=200. Cream limestone walls. SubTropolis fluorescent. Light level 10. Powered rails every 4 blocks (the climb is steep).

service_tunnel_contact_crossing.breccia_strip_dimensions: 1 block wide x 6 blocks long, on floor
service_tunnel_contact_crossing.notes: INSIDE THE SERVICE TUNNEL at the contact elevation Y=200. Walls transition visibly. 1-block-wide breccia strip on the floor. 3x5 alcove in upper (granite) wall with the composite terrane plaque. 6-7 oak signs of text. 1 redstone lamp on alcove ceiling. Dimmest point in the tunnel (light 8). Centerpiece #3 + Easter egg #1 + Easter egg #8 (breccia strip).

service_tunnel_granite_section.notes: Last 60 blocks of the service tunnel to Cheyenne end, lateral at Y=200. Pink granite walls. Cheyenne fluorescent. Light level 10. Powered rails every 4 blocks.

service_tunnel_cheyenne_end_checkpoint.blast_door_scale_note: Scaled 2x per the Cheyenne masterplan (real Cheyenne blast door is 3ft thick, 20ft tall; the build's door is 3 blocks thick, 12 blocks tall).
service_tunnel_cheyenne_end_checkpoint.blast_door_frame_dimensions: 6 blocks tall x 6 blocks wide (per cross-section)
service_tunnel_cheyenne_end_checkpoint.notes: Checkpoint corridor 4 blocks deep x 6 blocks wide. 25-ton blast door (3 thick x 6 wide x 12 tall) recessed in 4-block side branch. Beyond: 800-block J-curve. Light level 8-12. Centerpiece #1 + Easter egg #6 (U.S. Space Force sign).

composite_terrane_plaque.notes: 1x2 carved-stone plaque. 6-7 oak signs in 1x7 grid. Lit by 1 redstone lamp on alcove ceiling. Inside a 3x5x3 alcove carved into the upper (granite) wall of the 6x6 service tunnel. Centerpiece #3 / Easter egg #1. The build's Telling Detail - geologically honest (at a real geological boundary, not narrative fiction).

funicular.notes: 1-block gauge rail, single track, with passing loop at midpoint. Climb 600 blocks over 400 blocks of lateral distance at 1.5:1 grade.

summit_road.notes: Paved stone-brick road switchbacking down the south face. 6 switchbacks over 800 blocks of elevation, each switchback a 30-block horizontal traverse on a 5-block-wide shelf. Contact ring sign at Y=200 on the road.

summit_observation_platform.notes: Wooden platform on top of the summit station. 7th centerpiece of the build. 'Three Sites, One Mountain' sign (Easter egg #2) and rock identification chart (Easter egg #9) are placed here.

subtropolis_horizontal_portal.notes: 4x5 block opening in the limestone hillside at the south face of the mountain, at city level Y=0. The 1-block-wide polished diorite band directly above the frame at Y=200 is the visible surface expression of the contact. Centerpiece #5 + Easter egg #5 (World's Largest Underground Business Complex sign).

coastal_plain.notes: Sparse forest. Grand Avenue runs N-S at X=69 from world edge (Z=700) to city NE corner (Z=100). Stone brick for old town section (Z=350-700), granite-and-glass for new city section (Z=100-350).

cheyenne_chamber.notes: Per 01-masterplan. 1,319 half-ton coil springs under 15 spring-mounted buildings in 4.5-acre chamber. Bare granite walls, painted concrete floors, fluorescent lighting, 'dead air' feel.

subtropolis_chamber.notes: Per 02-masterplan. 200x200 chamber, 5x5 spec preserved as public shaft lift core. 15-mph speed limits, channel-letter signs, painted pillar numbers.

phases.name: Site Prep
phases.critical_risk: Build height must be >= 1,024 before first block; bedrock buffer at Y <= -220; coordinate axes agreed in writing.

phases.name: Continuous Mountain + Contact Ring
phases.critical_risk: Mountain bulk placement in two layers (limestone body, then granite cap on top) with contact ring at Y=200; NO ravine to carve out; switchback road connects city to SubTropolis portal.

phases.name: City + Houston Tunnel
phases.critical_risk: Public shaft buffer block in SE corner of Houston 24-block sample; T-markers at the 3 street-level entries (Wells Fargo, McKinney Garage, public shaft entrance).

phases.name: SubTropolis (Chamber + Sub-Basement + Horizontal Portal)
phases.critical_risk: Chamber excavation 200x200x100 in limestone; horizontal portal at (0, 0, -300) on the south face at city level with 1-block polished diorite band at Y=200 above the frame.

phases.name: Cheyenne (Chamber + J-Curve + Outer Portal)
phases.critical_risk: Outer portal at (0, 200, -420) on the south face at the contact elevation, in the granite; J-curve extension 50 blocks from chamber approach to outer portal.

phases.name: Public Shaft (Vertical Centerpiece)
phases.critical_risk: Shaft alignment: 7x7x100 from (60, 0, -70) to (60, -100, -100); mid-landing window at (60, -50, -70) must align with utility corridor 5 blocks east.

phases.name: Service Tunnel (Horizontal Centerpiece)
phases.critical_risk: Tunnel alignment: 6x6x120 from (-100, 0, -300) to (0, 200, -420), climbing 3.33:1; contact crossing at (-40, 200, -360); powered rail every 4 blocks in the climbing section.

phases.name: 25-Ton Blast Door + Composite Terrane Plaque
phases.critical_risk: Blast door scaled 2x (3x6x12) at (0, 200, -420); plaque in 3x5 alcove at (-40, 200, -360) with breccia strip on floor.

phases.name: Funicular + Summit Road (Return Route)
phases.critical_risk: NO SKYBRIDGE; funicular from (0, 200, -420) to (0, 800, -500) on 1.5:1 grade; summit road 6 switchbacks from (0, 800, -500) to (0, 0, 0); total return time ~13 min.

phases.name: Summit Observation Platform (7th Centerpiece)
phases.critical_risk: Platform on top of summit station at (0, 800, -500); 360-degree view of the world.

phases.name: Finishing (Easter Eggs, Lighting, Signage)
phases.critical_risk: All 9 easter eggs in place; lighting tuned; journey timing 30-45 min; return timing ~13 min; temporary markers removed.

centerpieces.name: 25-Ton Blast Door
centerpieces.block_spec: 3-block-thick x 6-block-wide x 12-block-tall (scaled 2x per Cheyenne masterplan) iron door in a quartz-stair frame, recessed in a 4-block side branch of the service tunnel terminus. 4-block-deep concrete-and-granite checkpoint corridor in front. Guard booth. 'U.S. Space Force' sign. 'Beyond this door' signs. Visible from the approaching minecart as a 1-block dark patch growing to a wall of iron.

centerpieces.name: Mid-Level Observation Landing
centerpieces.block_spec: 7x7 G-Cans-style observation room carved out of the south face of the public shaft at Y=-50. Single 3x3 glass pane window on south face looking out at city's underground utility corridor (parallel 7x7 shaft 5 blocks east at x=65). One labelled block of exposed limestone (Bethany Falls Limestone - 270 Ma, Pennsylvanian). Oak stairs bench. 4-line info sign. Iron door 2nd exit to emergency stair.

centerpieces.name: Composite Terrane Plaque
centerpieces.block_spec: 1x2 carved-stone plaque (chiseled calcite limestone half + chiseled stone brick granite half) in a 3x5x3 alcove carved into the upper (granite) wall of the 6x6 service tunnel at the contact crossing Y=200. 6-7 oak signs in 1x7 grid with the 7-line composite terrane text. Lit by 1 redstone lamp on alcove ceiling. 1-block-wide cobblestone + calcite breccia strip on the tunnel floor at the contact. Geologically honest at a real geological boundary.

centerpieces.name: Surface Entrance Pavilion (Public Shaft Top)
centerpieces.block_spec: 7x7 glass-and-steel pavilion at the city surface, in the NE corner of the city at the Combined Complex Transit Hub plaza. Glass pane walls on 3 sides, stone brick back wall housing lift machinery. Guard booth (oak fence + sign). Turnstile (iron bars). 'SubTropolis - Public Access' sign. 'EMPLOYEE ENTRANCE / EMERGENCY EGRESS' dual-use sign. T-marker at curb.

centerpieces.name: SubTropolis Horizontal Portal
centerpieces.block_spec: 4x5 block opening in the limestone hillside at the south face of the mountain, at city level (Y=0). Smooth stone frame with chiseled calcite corners; 1-block-wide polished diorite band directly above the frame at Y=200 (the visible surface expression of the contact). 'Hunt Midwest SubTropolis - Authorized Vehicles' sign + 'World's Largest Underground Business Complex' sign (Easter egg #5). Oak fence vehicle gate, 2 blocks wide. 6-block-wide asphalt road from portal mouth, switchbacking up the south face to the city plaza.

centerpieces.name: Cheyenne Outer Portal
centerpieces.block_spec: 6x6 opening in the granite, on the south face of the mountain, at the contact elevation Y=200. Concrete-and-granite frame with quartz-stair corners. 25-ton blast door (centerpiece #1) recessed in a 4-block side branch. 4-block concrete-and-granite checkpoint corridor. Guard booth. 'U.S. Space Force - Authorized Personnel Only' sign (Easter egg #6). 'Beyond this door' signs. Beyond the door: 800-block J-curve access tunnel to the chamber.

centerpieces.name: Summit Observation Platform (NEW 7th Centerpiece)
centerpieces.block_spec: 7x7 to 11x11 block wooden platform on top of the summit station at the granite summit (Y=800). Oak planks floor, spruce fence handrails (1-block tall) on all sides, oak stairs corner accents. Single oak sign at the center: 'Combined Complex - 800 m above sea level, 1.08 Ga granite'. The 'Three Sites, One Mountain' sign (Easter egg #2) and rock identification chart (Easter egg #9) are placed here. 360-degree view of the mountain, the city, the coastal plain, the SubTropolis horizontal portal, and the Cheyenne outer portal.

easter_eggs.name: Composite Terrane Plaque
easter_eggs.block_spec: 1x2 carved-stone plaque (chiseled calcite limestone half + chiseled stone brick granite half) in a 3x5x3 alcove in the upper (granite) wall of the 6x6 service tunnel at the contact crossing Y=200. 6-7 oak signs in 1x7 grid with the 7-line composite terrane text. 1 redstone lamp on alcove ceiling. 1-block-wide cobblestone + calcite breccia strip on the tunnel floor. The build's Telling Detail - geologically honest (at a real geological boundary, not narrative fiction).
plaque_text_lines: The granite above this alcove is 1.08 Ga Pikes Peak granite.
The limestone below is 270 Ma Bethany Falls limestone.
They are in horizontal contact at this elevation, where
the granite pluton pushed up through the limestone.
In real mountain ranges (the Alps, the Appalachians, Glacier National Park),
this is a common geological feature.

easter_eggs.name: Three Sites, One Mountain Sign
easter_eggs.block_spec: 3x3 oak sign panel on 1-block stone brick pedestal at the granite summit. 5 lines of text. Visible from the funicular arrival and the summit observation platform.
sign_text_lines: Cheyenne Mountain (Colorado Springs) - Granite, upper elevation
Houston Tunnels - City in the valley
Combined by horizontal contact at Y=200, connected by service tunnel

easter_eggs.name: Service Tunnel - Inspired by the Gotthard Base Tunnel
easter_eggs.block_spec: Oak sign at the SubTropolis end of the service tunnel. 'SBB CFF FFS' Swiss Federal Railways logo carved on 1-block chiseled calcite at the top-left of the gate frame. Subtle Gotthard reference.
sign_text_lines: Service Tunnel - Inspired by the Gotthard Base Tunnel (57 km, Switzerland)
SubTropolis-Cheyenne Service Tunnel: 0.12 km - not the longest, but the most climbed.

easter_eggs.name: Public Shaft - Inspired by the Helsinki Underground Master Plan
easter_eggs.block_spec: 'HELSINKI 5,500' carved on 1-block chiseled stone brick at the bottom of the public shaft. Oak sign on the wall with the dual-use / Helsinki reference.
sign_text_lines: Public Shaft - Inspired by the Helsinki Underground Master Plan
90 dual-use facilities, 5,500 civil-defense shelters, 1 million people capacity.

easter_eggs.name: World's Largest Underground Business Complex
easter_eggs.block_spec: Oak sign, black text, channel-letter-style at the SubTropolis horizontal portal, below the 'Hunt Midwest SubTropolis' sign.

easter_eggs.name: U.S. Space Force - Authorized Personnel Only
easter_eggs.block_spec: Oak sign, black text, military stencil at the Cheyenne outer portal arch + at the service tunnel entrance.

easter_eggs.name: Houston T-marker
easter_eggs.block_spec: 1-block red wool on white concrete at the public shaft entrance curb (inherited from 03-masterplan). Also at the 2 direct street-level tunnel entries (Wells Fargo and McKinney Garage). The visual signature of the world's civilian underground.

easter_eggs.name: Thrust-Fault Breccia Strip
easter_eggs.block_spec: 1-block-wide cobblestone + calcite strip, 1 block tall x 6 blocks long, on the FLOOR of the service tunnel at the contact crossing. The minecart rolls across it. no_ravine_summary.ravine_dropped: The V-shaped ravine from the previous design has been dropped. There is no gorge, no notch, no stream at the bottom of a ravine.
no_ravine_summary.replacement: The mountain is now one continuous mass with a horizontal granite-limestone contact at Y=200. The contact is visible on the south face of the mountain and is crossed by the service tunnel at the contact crossing.
no_ravine_summary.geological_honesty: The horizontal contact is real geology (granite plutons push up through limestone in mountain ranges worldwide). The composite terrane plaque is at the service tunnel contact crossing, where the tunnel walls visibly transition from cream limestone to pink granite.
